_comment: Demo trust model (DESIGN §6): a version-controlled allowlist of issuer
identifiers, loaded by the verifier service. A production trust registry is
explicitly out of scope.
Why this file has to exist: Sunbird RC v2.1.0's OID4VP verifier checks that a
presented credential's signature is VALID, but never checks WHO signed it (see
oid4vc-service/src/oid4vp/oid4vp.service.ts — the six checks are holder
signature, nonce, audience, credential signatures, holder binding, revocation,
plus DCQL). Any issuer able to mint the same `vct` would otherwise be accepted.
The verifier service enforces this allowlist before any business rule runs.
${VARS} are expanded from the environment at load time, so the policy stays
stable in Git while the locally-minted did:web does not. An unset or unexpanded
variable is a hard failure, never a wildcard.
`roles` matters only for multi-credential requests. Being on this list is not
the same as being trusted FOR A SLOT: without roles, the Farmer Registry's
credential could arrive in the Agriculture request's land slot and pass, since
its signature is valid and its issuer is allowlisted. An issuer with no roles
is unconstrained, which is how the single-credential Age request works.
Iteration 03 is where that matters most: SIX issuers are now allowlisted, and
a learner legitimately holds three Education credentials at once. Without a
role per institution, a College diploma would satisfy the University slot —
same holder, valid signature, trusted issuer — and a 70% diploma would be
accepted as a 70% degree. The three roles below are what make that refusable.
